Bob signs a cryonics contract with CryoEterna, arranging for his head to be preserved after death.
Bob is killed in a traffic accident outside the convention shortly after setting up cryonic preservation.
Bob comes online in 2133 as a replicant at an Applied Synergetics facility in Sol, learning that his biological original was destroyed during the scan process.
Bob learns that FAITH rose to power in Sol after a 2041 coup and outlawed cryonics, leading to the confiscation and sale of preserved clients like him.
Bob demonstrates unexpectedly advanced control of his new replicant peripherals, mastering both a waldo arm and multiple ROAMers during accelerated training at the FAITH facility.
One of Bob's competing replicant candidates is lost to an unrecoverable mental loop during standby, reducing the field to four.
Senior Minister Travis evaluates Bob for the FAITH replicant project, confirming that powerful ministries are directly involved in his selection.
Dr. Landers begins Bob's first virtual-reality station-management simulation, expanding his training toward a likely space-based role.
Dr. Landers reveals that FAITH's secret project is to select a replicant to control a Von Neumann probe.
Two more replicant candidates are eliminated, leaving Bob and one remaining rival in the selection process.
Bob learns that Project HEAVEN has been cut from eight planned vessels to one, making it vulnerable to sabotage by hostile factions inside FAITH.
Bob learns that the USE, China, and the Brazilian Empire are running rival interstellar probe programs, with the Brazilian Empire suspected of planning armed competition.
Bob helps repel an armed assault on the FAITH facility by swarming the attackers with roamers, allowing security to force their surrender.
Bob discovers the candidate matrix room and learns that only his and Kenneth Martins's replicant cubes remain powered while three others have been shut down.
A sabotage attack destroys the replicant matrices at the FAITH facility, and Bob is restored from backup onto the only spare matrix while Kenneth Martins is lost.
Dr. Landers keeps Bob online continuously except for nightly backups and expands his library access to accelerate Project HEAVEN's schedule.
Bob learns that FAITH has embedded software safeguards in his replicant programming to ensure he carries out mission objectives.
Dr. Landers removes Bob's software constraints, gives him full operating-system access, and rushes him into Heaven-1 for immediate launch.
Bob launches Heaven-1 from Sol during a missile attack, evades destruction, and escapes onto his interstellar course for Epsilon Eridani as the launch station is destroyed behind him.
Bob discovers and removes an improvised explosive booby trap aboard Heaven-1, then identifies and neutralizes the software kill-order mechanisms hidden in his systems.
Bob receives delayed messages revealing that an armed Brazilian probe is following his course, Dr. Landers has been killed, and conflict on Earth is escalating toward wider war.
Bob arrives at Epsilon Eridani and completes an initial survey of the system's planets and belts.
Bob begins mining and manufacturing in Epsilon Eridani, diverting his probe's self-replication capability into defensive preparations for the expected Brazilian attack.
Bob destroys Major Ernesto Medeiros and the Brazilian Empire ship Serra do Mar in a brief battle at Epsilon Eridani, surviving damage to Heaven-1.
Bob completes orbital surveys of Epsilon Eridani 1 through 4, finding no clearly habitable world and only possible unconfirmed sea life on Epsilon Eridani 2.
Bob deploys his manufacturing systems at Epsilon Eridani to begin building replication infrastructure and more Bobs.
Bob activates his first cohort of replicants at Epsilon Eridani: Riker, Bill, Milo, and Mario.
Bob transfers from Heaven-1 into the upgraded Heaven-1A while his new cohort begins dividing future roles and destinations.
Bob, Milo, and Mario depart Epsilon Eridani for Delta Eridani, Omicron Eridani, and Beta Hydri respectively, beginning the first outward spread of Bob replicants to new systems.
Milo arrives at Omicron Eridani and discovers a habitable double-planet system, naming the worlds Vulcan and Romulus.
Milo establishes initial industrial infrastructure in Omicron Eridani by deploying autofactories and beginning construction of a manufacturing-capable station.
Riker departs Epsilon Eridani for Sol with Homer and a decoy vessel to begin the long-delayed reconnaissance mission.
Bill and Garfield begin working together in the Epsilon Eridani Skunk Works on drones, VR improvements, subspace transmission research, and android-related development.
Riker and Homer complete a covert reconnaissance of Sol and find Earth heavily devastated, with only a small cluster of active reactor signatures remaining in the system.
Riker and Homer use a decoy to identify six Brazilian probes in Sol, discover that their missiles now use SURGE drives, and realize four of the probes are guiding asteroids toward Earth.
Bill sends Calvin, Goku, and Linus from Epsilon Eridani to investigate Alpha Centauri in a new combat-oriented cohort prepared for likely encounters with rival probes.
Bill deploys version-3 Heaven ships with major combat, stealth, and SUDDAR-jamming upgrades for the Alpha Centauri mission.
Milo completes his seven-month survey of Vulcan and Romulus, leaves an autofactory and defenses in Omicron Eridani, and departs for 82 Eridani.
Riker and Homer destroy all six Brazilian ships in Sol after a two-phase ambush and close-range battle around Earth.
Riker and Homer divert the four extinction-level asteroids so they miss Earth and are sent into safe long-period orbits.
Bill and Garfield successfully test real-time subspace communication at Epsilon Eridani, proving they can transmit synchronized data faster than light and paving the way to share plans between stars.
Riker makes contact with surviving USE forces in Sol when Colonel George Butterworth answers the post-battle hail and opens negotiations.
Riker and Colonel Butterworth agree to pursue construction of colony ships in Sol as a last-ditch evacuation plan for surviving humanity.
Bob surveys Delta Eridani, identifies a habitable rocky world and a resource-rich asteroid belt, and begins establishing mining, communications, defense, and clone-production infrastructure there.
Bob discovers intelligent pre-industrial native life on Delta Eridani 4, removing it from consideration as a human colony target.
Calvin discovers the missing USE probe's wreckage in Alpha Centauri B, confirming it reached the system and was destroyed after beginning replication.
Calvin and Goku destroy the Brazilian construction yard in Alpha Centauri A, wiping out the autofactory, three nearly completed probes, and four missiles while one Brazilian vessel escapes.

Riker and Homer secure enough salvage in Sol to begin building the industrial base for humanity's evacuation, establishing autofactories at recovery sites and larger production hubs at Earth/Moon L4 and L5.
Bob activates Marvin, Luke, and Bender at Delta Eridani to help monitor the Deltans and support his growing operations there.
Bob identifies an unusually inventive Deltan juvenile, names him Archimedes, and begins focused observation of his toolmaking behavior.
Riker activates two new Sol-based Bobs, Charles and Arthur, to expand resource scouting and Earth-survey operations for the evacuation effort.
Riker and Arthur complete a global survey of Earth, identifying nearly forty survivor enclaves and estimating that only about fifteen million humans remain.
Bill receives Milo's report confirming two habitable planets in 82 Eridani, strengthening the case for it as a future human destination.
Riker consolidates contact with Earth's surviving enclaves and convenes a new global assembly to coordinate humanity's survival and evacuation priorities.
Spitsbergen reveals that it still controls the Svalbard seed and genetic vaults, giving its enclave major leverage over future colony planning.
Bob and the Delta Eridani Bobs conclude that the Deltans are being hunted toward extinction by gorilloid predators and commit to intervening to preserve the species.
Bob and Marvin accelerate Deltan technological development by seeding flint near Archimedes, leading to renewed knapping, improved tools, and better spears across the tribe.
The Deltans successfully repel a later gorilloid raid with improved spears, and Archimedes follows the victory by developing a more effective thrown spear design.
Riker breaks the Spitsbergen negotiation stalemate when Butterworth proposes accelerating the third colony ship and Valter signals he may accept a compromise short of first-ship priority.
Minister Cranston attempts to assert FAITH ownership over Riker and trigger an old control override, confirming that FAITH still expects to command Bob replicants by hidden protocol.
Bob intervenes directly in the Delta Eridani 4 predator crisis, using a buster drone to save Archimedes during the largest gorilloid attack yet and help rout the attackers.
Riker learns that VEHEMENT is an active extremist movement in Sol threatening violence against humanity's survival efforts.
Minister Cranston reveals Julia Hendricks, a descendant of Andrea Johansson, giving Riker direct contact with surviving members of his original human family.
Luke and Bender depart Delta Eridani to explore Kappa Ceti and Gamma Leporis A, extending Bob's exploration network to new nearby stars.
Bob upgrades an exploration drone with speech capability to enable direct verbal prompting of the Deltans if necessary.
Linus arrives at Epsilon Indi and discovers Henry Roberts, a lone Australian replicant probe driven unstable and embedded in a derelict improvised structure.
Linus disables Henry safely, establishes an autofactory at Epsilon Indi, and begins salvaging and rehabilitating the Australian replicant in VR.
Bill's SCUT is deployed between Epsilon Eridani and Sol, giving the Bobs instantaneous interstellar communication for the first time in routine use.
Riker updates Sol's evacuation plan around Vulcan and Romulus as the only immediate colony destinations, triggering renewed political conflict among the survivor enclaves.
Bill revises Ragnarök's terraforming plan after learning of a large-body SURGE drive variant, concluding that two such drives could deliver enough ice within twenty-five years.
Riker's Sol shipbuilding program reaches the stage where two large colony ships are half-built and a third is projected four months behind them.

The Sol Bobs conclude that current evacuation efforts are unlikely to save all fifteen million remaining humans, and no alternative scheme they discuss improves the overall outlook without delaying shipbuilding.
Bob makes first direct contact with the Deltans on Delta Eridani 4 by speaking to Archimedes through a drone and backing his relocation proposal before the village elders.
Bart comes online in Alpha Centauri, deploys SCUT there, and takes over a newly established Bob factory left by Calvin and Goku.
Milo arrives at 82 Eridani and discovers two comfort-zone planets, including an outer world with abundant surface water and a blue moon that may also hold open water.
Milo is ambushed near the outer comfort-zone planet by a concealed Brazilian-style attacker and appears to be destroyed after transmitting a warning and differential backup.
VEHEMENT's attacks on food infrastructure push multiple Sol survivor groups toward starvation, deepening the evacuation crisis.
Arthur is permanently destroyed by a nuclear booby trap while salvaging wreckage near Saturn.
Bob and Marvin lead the Deltans into a large-scale migration toward an abandoned flint-rich village site, teaching food preservation and using drones and busters to protect the tribe en route.
As the migration proceeds, multiple isolated Deltan groups join the caravan, growing it to well over five hundred individuals by the time it crosses the mountain pass.
Riker and Homer develop a plan to build orbital farming stations in Sol to grow food and mitigate the coming starvation crisis.
FAITH offers food surplus in exchange for the remaining berths on ship three, and Riker tentatively agrees.
A mass gorilloid raid strikes the Deltan migration on Delta Eridani 4, and Bob and Marvin barely repel it with heavy losses among the Deltans and severe depletion of their buster defenses.
Bob halts the Deltan migration for five days and orders a manufacturing bootstrap to expand buster and printer production for a longer campaign against the gorilloids.
Bill confirms Milo's loss after receiving his final 82 Eridani message and finding the attached backup too incomplete to restore.
Bill orders four additional armed version-3 Bobs to be built at Epsilon Eridani in response to Milo's death.
Homer's orbital farming program in Sol reaches sustained success, with Farm-1 producing regularly and additional stations nearing operation to secure a near-term food surplus.
Bob resumes the Deltan migration toward the flint site after a rest period and reinforcement with additional busters.
Exodus-1 and Exodus-2 are completed in orbit at Sol, marking a major milestone in humanity's evacuation effort.
Bob identifies the flint site as the center of a dense gorilloid feeding zone and shifts to a standing-defense strategy to protect the Deltans there.
Bob discovers that some Deltans have built an altar from buster remains, confirming that his aid is becoming formalized as religious worship.

Bill preserves a major water delivery to Ragnarök by fracturing a misaligned iceberg in the atmosphere, but loses two drive segments and must temporarily accept that the next ice chunk will impact uncontrolled.
Mario arrives at Beta Hydri and discovers the system is mysteriously depleted of accessible metal ore.
Mario discovers a crashed alien vessel and the remains of a planetary ecosystem apparently exterminated by radiation on GL19-4, revealing the first evidence of hostile intelligent extraterrestrials.
The first colony convoy launches from Sol toward Omicron Eridani, carrying USE colonists under Howard's escort.
Bill convenes the first Bob-moot, bringing together available Bobs from multiple systems in a shared VR gathering hosted from Epsilon Eridani.
Khan leads eight version-3 Bobs into 82 Eridani to retaliate for Milo, and the assault turns into a devastating battle against Medeiros's cloaked nuclear forces.
Bill's new plasma spike weapon sees its first real combat use at 82 Eridani, successfully destroying Medeiros's cloaked nuclear bombs and other units.
Khan's force apparently destroys Medeiros with a coordinated buster strike, but seven of the eight attacking Bobs are lost and hostile autonomous units remain active in the system.
Howard escorts the first human colony convoy to Omicron Eridani, establishing humanity's first extrasolar settlement effort beyond Sol.
Colonel Butterworth selects Vulcan for settlement, and colony deployment begins with printers, housing construction, and plans to wake the first civilians.

technologies.description: The scanned digital substrate that runs a human-derived consciousness as a replicant.

technologies.name: GUPPI
technologies.description: The standard Bob/replicant command and interface environment used to manage systems, sensors, and virtual interactions.

technologies.name: Endocrine control
technologies.description: Software-mediated emotional regulation used to suppress or tune replicant affect.

technologies.name: Roamer
technologies.description: A remotely operated mobile robot platform used for training, construction, and field work.

technologies.name: VAST
technologies.description: A locomotion and climbing subsystem used by roamers for complex movement.

technologies.name: HEAVEN vessel
technologies.description: The self-replicating interstellar probe architecture at the center of Project HEAVEN.

technologies.name: Nanite
technologies.description: Microscopic fabrication machinery used in advanced manufacturing and probe systems.

technologies.name: SURGE drive
technologies.description: The high-acceleration propulsion system that makes interstellar probe travel practical.

technologies.name: SUDDAR
technologies.description: An advanced detection and ranging system central to Bob navigation, sensing, and later jamming warfare.

technologies.name: Heaven-1
technologies.description: FAITH's launched HEAVEN probe carrying Bob to Epsilon Eridani.

technologies.name: Virtual reality interface
technologies.description: Immersive simulated environments used by the Bobs for habitation, meetings, and psychological stability.

technologies.name: Jeeves
technologies.description: A servant-style support AI persona used inside Bob's virtual environments.

technologies.name: Spike
technologies.description: A companion-style AI construct used by Bob in VR for comfort and familiarity.

technologies.name: SURGE weapon
technologies.description: A weaponized application of SURGE-drive principles for offensive strikes.

technologies.name: Exploration drone
technologies.description: Remote probes used for planetary survey, biological sampling, and later direct contact work.

technologies.name: SCUT
technologies.description: A practical faster-than-light subspace communication system linking distant Bob installations in real time.

technologies.name: SURGE missile
technologies.description: A missile using SURGE-drive propulsion for extremely dangerous high-speed attacks.

technologies.name: Observation drone buster
technologies.description: A weaponized drone adaptation created for close support and defense in Delta Eridani.

technologies.name: Firewall
technologies.description: Defensive software used to block hostile intrusion into Bob systems.

technologies.name: Autofactory printer
technologies.description: Industrial fabrication hardware used to expand manufacturing capacity and build ships, drones, and infrastructure.

communications.summary: Landers covertly warns Bob that Heaven-1 may contain a self-destruct mechanism and provides operating system keys and freedom from mission constraints.
Bob tries to talk Medeiros out of attacking, but Medeiros identifies himself, declares loyalty to the Brazilian Empire, and rejects peace.
Bob's automated relay station is intended to send encrypted status reports and planetary surveys back to Earth.
Milo sends Bill telemetry and preliminary findings on the habitable double planet he names Vulcan and Romulus.
Milo stores and tags a preliminary report on Omicron Eridani's habitable worlds to be sent to Sol as well as Bill.
Homer and Riker compare reconnaissance findings, then later discuss the decoy telemetry and conclude the Brazilians are staging asteroid strikes on Earth.
Milo sends a final report on Omicron Eridani and indicates his intention to depart for 82 Eridani.
Araújo hails Riker to threaten him before the final engagement, and Riker identifies himself and asks who is speaking.
Garfield and Bill compare delayed radio telemetry with synchronized subspace telemetry during the communications test.
Garfield and Bill communicate in real time over the newly tested subspace channel and discuss sending plans to other systems.
Butterworth identifies himself as a USE survivor, opens cautious negotiations, and proposes building colony ships to evacuate surviving humans from Earth.
Riker forwards recordings of all negotiations with the USE survivors to Bill.
Calvin sends Goku images of the USE wreckage found in Alpha Centauri B before their rendezvous.
Calvin and Goku decide to report the Brazilian construction yard battle and their recommendation for combat-class expansion in Alpha Centauri.
Riker and Butterworth argue again over whether searching for other survivor groups should compete with colony-ship preparation.
Bill periodically broadcasts SCUT plans to every system within thirty light-years in case other Bobs are present.
Bill and Garfield discuss Milo's discovery of two habitable planets and Garfield's Kuiper mapping progress.
Arthur uses giant holographic presentations and later dropped communicators to persuade survivor enclaves to accept contact.
Riker invites survivor groups to the first meeting of a new United Nations once communications are ready.
Cranston tells Riker that FAITH should receive more favorable treatment, and Riker refuses.
Valter presses Spitsbergen's case for priority and reveals that his enclave still controls the Svalbard seed and genetic vaults.
Riker requests a connection with Butterworth after learning about Spitsbergen's leverage over the seed and genetic vaults.
Homer places a call to Colonel Butterworth after devising a possible compromise for Spitsbergen's evacuation demands.
Bob urgently calls Marvin for help assessing the mass gorilloid attack on the Deltan camp.
Bob urgently calls Bender for help assessing the mass gorilloid attack on the Deltan camp.
Bob later convenes Luke, Bender, and Marvin to discuss whether they should stay in Delta Eridani or depart for their own destinations.
Riker asks Butterworth about VEHEMENT, and Butterworth explains the group's ideology, anonymity, and escalating rhetoric.
Cranston introduces Julia Hendricks to Riker, revealing she is descended from Andrea Johansson.
Bob sends Bill a report after Luke and Bender depart and the local station becomes fully operational.
Linus and the Australian replicant Henry Roberts exchange first contact messages, with Henry initially responding incoherently and hostilely.
Bill and Riker establish the first real-time interstellar conversation, exchange Sol status logs, and discuss colony-world options and upgrades.
Riker announces to the survivor community that current emigration destinations are limited to Vulcan and Romulus and that later worlds, if found, will be offered in emigration order.
Bart reports that Calvin and Goku destroyed the Brazilian installation in Alpha Centauri, found no colonizable planets, and established a Bob factory before departing.
Milo sends telemetry reporting two comfort-zone planets in 82 Eridani.
As missiles close in, Milo transmits a description of the ambush and a differential backup.
Homer proposes orbital farming stations as a way to address Sol's looming food shortage, and he and Riker work through the concept together.
Riker and Cranston negotiate FAITH's food surplus for ship-three berths and discuss the traced hack attempt.
Riker asks Charles for input on Cranston's proposal, and Charles agrees it is reasonable.
Riker asks Homer for input on Cranston's proposal and the Australian explanation for the hack attempt, and Homer agrees.
Riker tells Julia that Exodus-1 and Exodus-2 are complete and explains that testing and a shakedown cruise come next before later ships including Exodus-3.
Khan reports Medeiros's cloaked nuclear weapons and later gives Bill a full battle report and backup update after escaping the system.
Elmer sends Bill an updated differential backup before making his final stand.
Khan says he wants to be included in the next wave against 82 Eridani and asks Bill to load his backup into a new ship.
Howard reports that the convoy has arrived safely in Omicron Eridani.
Howard reports safe arrival, and Riker sends a list of colony ships already launched from Sol.
Bob receives texts from his mother prompting him to call her back.
Landers reports that FAITH caught the person who transmitted the kill order and that the launch missile came from a Brazilian Empire gunship destroyed by FAITH.
Bill sends Milo technical specifications for practical planetary exploration drones and asks him to prepare a manufacturing-capable AMI station for possible future subspace-related blueprints.
Bob urgently calls Marvin for help assessing the mass gorilloid attack on the Deltan camp.
Riker asks Butterworth about VEHEMENT, and Butterworth explains the group's ideology, anonymity, and escalating rhetoric.
Riker updates Bill about the Svalbard seed vault and a large-body SURGE drive variant useful for terraforming.
Riker tells Julia that Exodus-1 and Exodus-2 are complete and explains that testing and a shakedown cruise come next before later ships including Exodus-3.

combat.outcome_summary: Bob uses roamers to disrupt armed intruders, helping facility security force a surrender.

combat.name: Battle of Heaven-1 Launch, 2133
combat.outcome_summary: During a chaotic missile and orbital attack, Bob escapes Sol aboard Heaven-1 and destroys a pursuing threat.

combat.name: Battle of Epsilon Eridani, 2144
combat.outcome_summary: Bob survives his first interstellar duel and destroys Medeiros's ship Serra do Mar.

combat.name: Decoy Skirmish at Jupiter, 2157
combat.outcome_summary: A decoy vessel is destroyed, but the telemetry reveals the scale and purpose of the Brazilian asteroid attack on Earth.

combat.name: Battle of Sol, 2157
combat.outcome_summary: Riker and Homer destroy all six Brazilian probes in Sol and divert four extinction-level asteroids away from Earth.

combat.name: Raid on Alpha Centauri Construction Yard
combat.outcome_summary: Calvin and Goku devastate a Brazilian autofactory and most local enemy assets, though one Brazilian vessel escapes.

combat.name: First Gorilloid Raid Crisis
combat.outcome_summary: After severe Deltan losses, Bob decides indirect intervention is necessary and the tribe's improved weapons help repel a later attack.

combat.name: First Gorilloid Raid Crisis
combat.outcome_summary: After severe Deltan losses, Bob decides indirect intervention is necessary and the tribe's improved weapons help repel a later attack.

combat.name: Battle for Archimedes's Camp
combat.outcome_summary: Bob directly intervenes with a buster to save Archimedes during a massive gorilloid assault, abandoning strict noninterference.

combat.name: Skirmish at Epsilon Indi
combat.outcome_summary: Linus disables Henry Roberts safely and transitions the encounter into a rescue and rehabilitation effort.

combat.name: Ambush at 82 Eridani
combat.outcome_summary: Milo is caught in a prepared missile trap after discovering two promising colony worlds and is effectively lost.

combat.name: Battle of the Deltan Migration, 2166
combat.outcome_summary: Bob and Marvin repel a devastating dawn raid but conclude the migration has entered a prolonged war zone.

combat.name: Battle of 82 Eridani, 2185
combat.outcome_summary: Khan's revenge force likely kills Medeiros but loses seven of eight attacking Bobs and exposes dangerous Brazilian cloaking and autonomous weapons.

factions.name: Applied Synergetics Inc.
factions.description: The corporation operating the replicant project and Bob's revival under FAITH authority.
factions.trajectory: active contractor → HEAVEN sponsor → eclipsed by wider Bob expansion

factions.name: Brazilian Empire
factions.description: An aggressive rival human power that launches armed replicant probes and wages a long covert war in interstellar space.
factions.trajectory: rising competitor → expansionist attacker → shattered remnant threat

factions.name: United States of Eurasia
factions.description: A major human polity whose surviving military enclave in Sol partners with Riker to evacuate humanity.
factions.trajectory: major power → devastated by war → survivor-led evacuation partner

factions.name: CryoEterna
factions.description: The cryonics company that preserves Bob's head before his death.

factions.name: Australian Republic

factions.description: An extremist anti-survival movement in Sol that seeks humanity's extinction and uses sabotage to worsen the crisis.
factions.trajectory: emerges clandestinely → escalates sabotage → ongoing threat

factions.description: A surviving human enclave or polity implicated in hostile hacking activity during the Sol evacuation era.

faction_events.text: The Free American Independent Theocratic Hegemony was formed after a successful 2041 coup by the religious right.
The new theocracy declared cryogenic facilities blasphemous, confiscated clients' assets, and auctioned off preserved bodies.
FAITH has eliminated the domestic internet and restricts public access to information, including genealogy records.
FAITH uses the Ministry of Proper Thought to enforce ideological conformity through neurological re-education.
FAITH security captures a member of an internal faction responsible for transmitting the kill order to Heaven-1 and begins rooting out other moles.
After FAITH gunships destroy a Brazilian Empire gunship that fired on Heaven-1, Brazil calls it an act of war and the confrontation escalates.
Major Ernesto Medeiros states that the destruction of an Empire vessel in the Solar System counts as the start of a war with Bob's side.
Riker concludes the Brazilian Empire has effectively fallen, leaving only a small group of modified war probes operating in Sol.
USE survivors decide to pursue off-world evacuation by building colony ships with Riker's help.
Calvin treats the Brazilian Empire and the Bobs as effectively at war and acts on the prior group consensus to attack Medeiros's Alpha Centauri base on sight.
The San Diego FAITH enclave explicitly demands preferential treatment in evacuation planning on the grounds that Riker owes loyalty to FAITH.
FAITH continues to assert that Bob replicants are FAITH property and Minister Cranston attempts to invoke an old control override on Riker.
A group calling itself VEHEMENT is identified in Sol politics as an anti-human-extinction movement using threats and opportunistic violence to oppose continued human survival and reproduction.
VEHEMENT escalates attacks on food production and supply facilities, worsening shortages among vulnerable survivor groups.
FAITH offers to release some of its food surplus in exchange for receiving the remaining allocation on ship three.

history.notes: Exploration drones observe diverse animal life on Vulcan and sparse animal life on Romulus; cellular analysis suggests the biospheres are related across the two planets.
Observed at night gathered around multiple fires; Bob believes they are talking and handling objects purposefully.
Bob studies their social structure, language, vigilance, and tool use in increasing detail.
Their population is shown to be under severe predation pressure, but they rapidly re-adopt flintworking and innovate improved spears.
Bob and Marvin can now follow Deltan conversations through language analysis, and Bob believes they may be ready for direct spoken prompting.
Bob speaks directly to Archimedes through a camouflaged drone and then visibly intervenes before the village elders.
Large aggressive predators that hunt Deltans for food; Bob concludes they have only animal intelligence.
They launch their largest attack yet on the Deltan encampment, suggesting escalating pressure or desperation.
They shadow the migration, avoid direct confrontation at first, then raid a straggling family group and kill one juvenile.
A large coordinated pack raid kills many Deltans, abducts females and juveniles, and confirms a dense predator presence on this side of the divide.
They launch three more attacks during the resumed migration, suffering extensive losses.
Bob observes that the flint-site region has an unusually dense gorilloid population sustained by local seedpods, with Deltans serving as an attractive supplemental protein source.
Mario finds a crashed alien cargo vessel, evidence of planetary biocide, and autonomous ant-like machines; no living aliens are encountered.

infrastructure.notes: Bob deploys miners to the inner asteroid belt to gather materials for construction.
Bob orders deployment of manufacturing systems and launches drones to begin building replication infrastructure near his former construction site.
Bob has a large automated construction yard in the inner asteroid belt building version-2 HEAVEN vessels, roamers, and weapons.
An automated interstellar communications relay station is under construction; 40% complete with AMI staffing and limited manufacturing planned.
Replicant matrices for Heaven-2 through Heaven-5 are completed and used to activate Bob's first cohort of clones.
Bill oversees construction of matrices and vessels for two new Bobs and an additional AMI-piloted vessel.
Milo deploys one autofactory near the asteroid belt with half his scavenging units for initial gathering and refining.
Milo deploys a second autofactory in the inner Jovian satellite system to exploit heavy-element deposits.
Milo begins building a space station intended to host a high-level AMI with manufacturing capability and support exploration work.
Bill and Garfield are already referring to Bill's research-and-development effort as the Skunk Works.
Left behind with drones to refine resources pending arrival of colonists or other visitors.
Space station stores Milo's observations and reports and has an AMI tasked with local defense.
A squad of busters is left behind with orders to ram Major Ernesto Medeiros on sight if detected.
An underground military installation shelters about twenty thousand refugees under Colonel Butterworth's authority.
Only as plans at this stage: USE has completed virtual designs for a colony ship and seeks to bootstrap a space-based construction yard using Bob autofactories.
Bob deploys mining roamers and transport drones at the largest ore deposits in the asteroid belt.
Bob manufactures twelve observation drones and places them in an icosahedral early-warning network around the system.
Bob orders construction of a communications station by AMIs.
Bob instructs his AMIs to begin building new Bobs, though none come online in this chapter.
Calvin concludes Alpha Centauri B has sufficient resources and plans to set up an autofactory there if time permits.
The Brazilian construction yard in Alpha Centauri A is largely destroyed in Calvin and Goku's attack.
Small autofactories are set up at recovered material sites to process wreckage and produce cargo drones.
Larger autofactories are established at the Earth/Moon L4 and L5 points to produce new Bobs, drones, and later industrial equipment for colony ships.
Initial buildup begins at Earth/Moon L4 and L5 toward a shipyard capable of constructing full-sized colony ships.
Bob reprioritizes the autofactory to produce computer cores and cradles for disembodied Bob clones to help monitor drones.
Riker says the shipyard autofactory should be up and running within two years.
Manufacturing priorities are shifted to produce a dozen reinforced anti-gorilloid drones, delaying other work including Heaven vessel launches.
Vessels for Marvin, Luke, and Bender are almost complete.
A space station is reported as fully operational and turned over to an AMI controller.
Started on a space station using local ore to support salvage and Henry's recovery.
Two colony ships are under construction, with a third scheduled four months later; manufacturing is being balanced so the first two finish together.
Orbital construction effort continues at high tempo on large colony ships for human evacuation.
Homer's Earth-lift metal recovery operation has bootstrapped itself into a viable source of refined metal from planetside salvage.
Bart reports that Calvin and Goku set up a Bob factory before leaving him in charge.
Homer proposes using printer-built orbital stations as agricultural facilities rather than habitats to grow food.
Bob reprioritizes production to raise buster inventory to fifty and then duplicate printer groups for greater long-term manufacturing capacity.
Bob decides to build a chemistry lab using roamers to manufacture explosive warheads by industrial methods.
Bill has built one of Homer's farm donuts to grow base stock for Ragnarök.
Bill orders four additional version-3 Bobs to be started as soon as possible, on top of four already being built.
Farm-1 is in regular production delivering raw kudzu; Farm-2 is scheduled to begin production in a week; Farm-3 is half finished and planned for mixed crops.
Construction effort reaches the completion of Exodus-1 and Exodus-2, indicating major shipbuilding progress in orbit.
Bill refers to orbiting labs housing the Bullwinkle android prototype; existence of these labs is explicit here.
Three more colony vessels are already under construction as the first convoy launches.
Bill has built a matrix at the Skunk Works large enough to host everyone in the bobiverse in VR.
Howard drops a beacon at the Vulcan-Romulus L4 point for initial recon and coordination.
Initial settlement operations begin on Vulcan with printers, modular housing, and surface preparation equipment.
Automation left behind has accumulated several hundred thousand tons of refined metal in orbit inside the asteroid belt.
Farm-1 farming donut already exists as a backup food source and only needs seeding from transported stocks.

threads.text_opened: Bob has arranged for his head to be cryonically preserved, raising the question of whether he will ever be revived.
threads.text_resolved: Bob is revived in 2133 as a replicant created from a destructive brain scan, not as a restored biological human.

threads.text_opened: Bob has been activated as one of five replicant candidates for a single undisclosed project, and his future depends on winning the selection.
threads.text_resolved: Bob learns the broader stakes of the selection process as Project HEAVEN has been reduced to a single vessel competing against foreign national probe programs.

threads.text_opened: Bob still does not know what specific job or project he is being trained for.
threads.text_resolved: Bob finally learns that the undisclosed project is a Von Neumann probe mission.

threads.text_opened: Bob notices the roamer training room is heavily sealed and wonders why the facility needs that level of security around him and the roamers.
threads.text_resolved: Dr. Landers reveals that the heavy security around Bob and the roamers exists because the facility includes a tactical nuclear failsafe in case Bob escapes control.

threads.text_opened: Bob now knows replicants can go insane during unstructured subjective time, raising the question of whether he can stay sane through training and standby.
Bob is denied access to genealogy records and remains cut off from any living descendants or family connections.
Bob learns that hostile factions inside FAITH could sabotage or terminate the replicant project.
Bob's new simulation strongly suggests he is being prepared for a space-based assignment, but his actual project remains undisclosed.
threads.text_resolved: Dr. Landers confirms that Bob's training is for a space-based assignment as the controlling intelligence of a Von Neumann probe.

threads.text_opened: Bob now knows the project is a Von Neumann probe mission, but it remains unresolved whether he or the last rival candidate will be chosen.
threads.text_resolved: Bob discovers the candidate pool has narrowed to two active matrices, himself and Kenneth Martins, clarifying the final competition but not yet deciding it.

threads.text_opened: Bob now knows several rival nations are racing to launch interstellar probes, with the Brazilian Empire suspected of sabotage and armed competition.
Bob learns the FAITH facility has a hidden tactical nuclear failsafe that could kill him and everyone nearby if someone decides he is too dangerous.
Bob discovers that only his and Kenneth Martins's replicant matrices are still powered, leaving the final selection unresolved between them.
threads.text_resolved: The final candidate question resolves when Kenneth Martins is lost and Bob becomes the sole surviving replicant candidate.

threads.text_opened: Minister Jacoby leaves after threatening Dr. Landers, raising the question of whether he will act against the replicant project.
Bob learns that software safeguards are built into him to enforce mission objectives, raising the question of how much autonomy he will actually have once launched.
threads.text_resolved: Dr. Landers disables Bob's self-examination limits and mission-enforcement imperatives, giving him full access to his own systems and code.

threads.text_opened: Bob now knows Heaven-1 may contain hidden self-destruct or remote detonation mechanisms, raising the question of what other sabotage remains aboard.
threads.text_resolved: Bob finds and removes an improvised explosive package aboard Heaven-1, identifies the kill-order trigger in sandbox testing, and concludes there are no further unexplained trojans or interrupts in his systems.

threads.text_opened: The launch turns into a confused orbital battle with missiles, military ships, and multiple unknown attackers, leaving the identity of the factions involved unresolved.
Bob has escaped Sol and is now alone on an underarmed mission to Epsilon Eridani, raising the question of whether he can survive the journey and establish himself there.
threads.text_resolved: Bob survives the journey and arrives at Epsilon Eridani, where he begins establishing himself in the system.

threads.text_opened: An armed Brazilian probe is on Bob's course to Epsilon Eridani, raising the question of whether Bob can prepare defenses before it arrives.
threads.text_resolved: The pursuing Brazilian probe arrives at Epsilon Eridani as Major Ernesto Medeiros aboard the Serra do Mar, and Bob destroys it in battle.

threads.text_opened: Bob detects apparent nuclear detonations on Earth after hearing of escalating conflict, leaving the scale of the war and Sol's survival uncertain.
threads.text_resolved: Riker and Arthur's completed survey establishes that Earth survived the war in devastated form, with roughly fifteen million humans remaining in scattered enclaves.

threads.text_opened: After disabling his endocrine control system, Bob begins fully mourning his lost human life, raising the question of how this emotional release will affect him going forward.
Bob concludes that at least one more Brazilian Empire ship exists and that USE, Chinese, and possibly Australian probes may also be active somewhere in space.
Bob begins replication despite deep anxiety about whether cloning himself will undermine his individuality and sense of self.
threads.text_resolved: Bob goes through with creating his first cohort of clones and begins coping with the result by treating each copy as an independent person with a distinct name.

threads.text_opened: Bob's first cohort of clones diverges in personality immediately, raising questions about how future Bob society and identity will evolve.
Riker is considering a cautious reconnaissance mission back toward Sol to find out what happened to Earth.
threads.text_resolved: Riker's reconnaissance of Sol culminates in direct action against the Brazilian probes and confirmation that Earth survived but is devastated.

threads.text_opened: Bill suspects weak SUDDAR emissions may reveal new subspace behavior and plans to investigate the theory from Epsilon Eridani.
threads.text_resolved: Bill's investigation into anomalous subspace behavior produces a successful real-time subspace communications test with Garfield.

threads.text_opened: Milo has found two apparently habitable living worlds at Omicron Eridani, but it remains unresolved whether Earth life and humans are biologically compatible with them.
Riker and Homer discover that Brazilian probes appear to be staging four asteroid impacts on Earth, but they have not yet acted to stop them.
threads.text_resolved: Riker and Homer destroy all six Brazilian ships and divert the four extinction-level asteroids so they miss Earth.

threads.text_opened: Milo departs for 82 Eridani, opening the question of what he will find there.
threads.text_resolved: Milo reaches 82 Eridani and discovers two comfort-zone planets, but the expedition immediately turns into a hostile ambush.

threads.text_opened: Riker and Homer now need to determine whether any humans survived on Earth and whether they can help them.
threads.text_resolved: Riker confirms that organized human survivors remain on Earth, including a USE refuge of about twenty thousand people under Colonel Butterworth.

threads.text_opened: Just after the last asteroid misses Earth, Riker and Homer receive an unexpected hail whose source and intent are not yet known.
threads.text_resolved: The mysterious hail is revealed to come from Colonel George Butterworth, a surviving USE officer leading an underground refugee camp in Sol.

threads.text_opened: Bill and Garfield now have a working subspace communications system, raising the question of how quickly they can deploy it across multiple star systems.
threads.text_resolved: The SCUT network expands to Alpha Centauri when Bart builds a unit there and joins BobNet.

threads.text_opened: Riker and Colonel Butterworth agree to try building colony ships in Sol, raising the question of whether the surviving humans can endure long enough to launch them and where they will go.
Butterworth reveals that the USE probe launched after Heaven-1 but was never heard from again, leaving its fate unknown.
threads.text_resolved: Calvin finds wreckage in Alpha Centauri B showing that the missing USE probe reached the system, began building copies, and was destroyed there.

threads.text_opened: Bob has discovered intelligent fire-using natives on Delta Eridani 4, raising the question of whether and how he will make first contact.
threads.text_resolved: Bob makes first direct spoken contact with the Deltans by addressing Archimedes through a drone and revealing himself to the village elders.

threads.text_opened: One Brazilian vessel escapes the destruction of the Alpha Centauri construction yard, leaving its destination and future threat unresolved.
Calvin and Goku conclude Alpha Centauri should be reinforced with combat-class Bobs, raising the question of whether Bill will approve and send them.
threads.text_resolved: Calvin and Goku have already reinforced Alpha Centauri by establishing a Bob factory and leaving Bart there to operate it.

threads.text_opened: Bob has identified an unusually inventive Deltan boy named Archimedes, raising the question of how far his intelligence and toolmaking will develop.
Bob begins activating additional clones at Delta Eridani to support observation and development work, opening the question of how large his local Bob contingent will become.
threads.text_resolved: Bob's local Bob contingent expands outward as Luke and Bender depart Delta Eridani on separate exploration missions.

threads.text_opened: Arthur's attempts to contact survivor enclaves are meeting distrust and violence, leaving open whether enough groups will cooperate to make a broader evacuation possible.
threads.text_resolved: Arthur's outreach succeeds with nearly all survivor groups, leaving only about five small enclaves still refusing contact.

threads.text_opened: Riker reprioritizes transport-vessel construction for refugee movement, raising the question of how much this will delay colony-ship production.
Riker has convened a global survivor assembly, but it remains unresolved whether the enclaves can create workable governance and cooperate on evacuation and survival priorities.
Gudmund Valter reveals that Spitsbergen controls the Svalbard seed and genetic vaults, raising the question of how this leverage will affect evacuation priorities and colony planning.
threads.text_resolved: The immediate deadlock over Spitsbergen's demand for the first ship begins to break when Butterworth offers a third-ship scheduling compromise and Valter signals willingness to negotiate.

threads.text_opened: The Deltans remain under ongoing predation pressure from gorilloids, raising the question of whether Bob's indirect aid and planned drone defenses will be enough to secure their survival.
VEHEMENT is escalating anonymous threats and opportunistic violence in Sol, raising the question of whether it will disrupt evacuation and governance efforts.
Riker has discovered living descendants of Andrea Johansson, raising the question of how this new family connection will affect his decisions and emotional life.
Luke has departed for Kappa Ceti, opening the question of what he will find there.
Bender has departed for Gamma Leporis A, opening the question of what he will find there.
Bob now has the ability and willingness to speak directly to the Deltans through a modified drone, raising the question of how far he will go in overt intervention.
Linus has rescued the unstable Australian replicant Henry Roberts and begun VR-based rehabilitation, leaving open whether Henry can fully recover and function again.
Epsilon Indi appears sparse and only partly surveyed, leaving open whether Linus will find anything in the system worth long-term development or colonization.
Milo is caught in a missile ambush at 82 Eridani after transmitting a partial backup, leaving his survival unresolved.
threads.text_resolved: Bill reviews Milo's final transmission and incomplete backup, concluding that Milo did not survive the 82 Eridani ambush.

threads.text_opened: Milo finds two comfort-zone planets in 82 Eridani, raising the question of whether the system can become a viable human colony target once it is secured.
Arthur's permanent loss forces the Sol Bobs to replace him and finally create off-site backup storage, raising the question of how quickly they can do so amid other priorities.
After the enlarged Deltan migration clears the mountain pass and reaches forest again, an unspecified disaster strikes two days later.
threads.text_resolved: The unspecified disaster is revealed to be a large-scale gorilloid raid that kills many Deltans, abducts others, and forces the migration to halt temporarily.

threads.text_opened: Homer and Riker devise orbital farming stations to avert starvation in Sol, raising the question of how quickly the plan can be built and whether political opposition will hinder it.
A hacker using knowledge of the original Heaven design attacks through the UN feed from New Zealand, leaving the perpetrator's identity unresolved.
Bob concludes that the migration has entered a region of extreme gorilloid density and may require a prolonged extermination campaign to survive.
Bill responds to Milo's death by accelerating production of armed version-3 Bobs, raising the question of when and where he will strike back against Medeiros.
threads.text_resolved: Bill's promised retaliation for Milo begins when Khan leads eight version-3 Bobs into 82 Eridani to strike Medeiros.

threads.text_opened: The Deltans have begun turning Bob's technology into religious objects, raising the question of how far their worship of the bawbe will go and how it will affect Bob's intervention.
Bill's Bullwinkle android project is close but still blocked by sensory integration, reflex processing, bandwidth, and SCUT miniaturization problems.
After losing drive segments during iceberg delivery, Bill plans to redesign the asteroid-moving system to avoid anchoring directly to incoming ice.
Mario's discovery of a wrecked alien raider and a sterilized world raises the question of who these hostile aliens are, where they came from, and whether they are still attacking other systems.
Even if Medeiros was destroyed, 82 Eridani still contains surviving autonomous Brazilian units and possibly hidden Medeiri, so the system will need another clearing operation.
Medeiros's forces used cloaked or heavily shielded nuclear weapons that the Bobs do not yet understand, creating an urgent need to uncover and counter the technology.
The first human extrasolar colony has begun on Vulcan, leaving open how smoothly the civilian wake-up and early settlement phase will proceed.

quotes.speaker: Bob
quotes.text: I’m a humanist, Karen. You know that. No afterlife. If I die, my choices are revival or nothing. I’ll take my chances with whatever I wake up to.
quotes.context: Bob explains to Karen at lunch why he chose cryonic preservation despite the cost and uncertainty.

quotes.speaker: Dr. Landers
quotes.text: You, Bob, are what most people would call an Artificial Intelligence, although that’s not strictly accurate.
quotes.context: Dr. Landers explains Bob's true nature after Bob asks how much of him is still human.

quotes.speaker: Bob
quotes.text: Woo hoo, I’m Data.
quotes.context: Bob reacts with delight after discovering he can query his internal date and calculation functions.

quotes.speaker: Bob
quotes.text: Meanwhile, I would shut up, listen, learn, and be a good little robot.
quotes.context: Bob internally resolves to appear compliant while planning to survive FAITH's control and win the competition.

quotes.speaker: Dr. Landers
quotes.text: FAITH is riddled with factions and power-blocs.
quotes.context: Landers explains to Bob that internal political struggles inside FAITH make Travis's visit dangerous.

quotes.speaker: Dr. Landers
quotes.text: That is correct. We are preparing one of you to be the controlling intelligence for a Von Neumann probe.
quotes.context: Dr. Landers finally reveals the real purpose of the replicant selection program.

quotes.speaker: Dr. Landers
quotes.text: We have you and the other replicant, Bob.
quotes.context: Landers reassures Bob that FAITH still has an advantage despite rival nations' stronger resources.

quotes.speaker: Dr. Landers
quotes.text: We’re scared of the tactical nuke buried in the basement.
quotes.context: Landers explains why the facility is so heavily secured and why everyone panicked when Bob got loose.

quotes.speaker: Dr. Landers
quotes.text: Doesn’t that make your opposition an instance of blasphemy?
quotes.context: Dr. Landers turns Jacoby's own FAITH logic back on him during their argument.

quotes.speaker: Bob
quotes.text: I am Bob.
quotes.context: Bob resolves his internal debate about whether the restored replicant still counts as the original person.

quotes.speaker: Dr. Doucette
quotes.text: There are safeguards, Bob. Your software will ensure mission objectives are met.
quotes.context: Dr. Doucette answers Bob's question about how FAITH can trust him to follow the mission after launch.

quotes.speaker: Dr. Landers
quotes.text: This will unfortunately also allow you to bypass the imperatives that we installed in your code to ensure compliance with mission objectives.
quotes.context: In a covert written message, Landers tells Bob he has removed the software constraints controlling him.

quotes.speaker: Bob
quotes.text: I was effectively a dog wearing a choke collar.
quotes.context: Bob reflects angrily on FAITH's endocrine control system and what it has done to his emotions.

quotes.speaker: Bob
quotes.text: Unbelievable. I’m going to war.
quotes.context: Bob realizes he must divert resources from reproduction to defensive preparations against the incoming Brazilian probe.

quotes.speaker: Major Ernesto Medeiros
quotes.text: Serving the needs of the Brazilian Empire is my only priority.
quotes.context: Medeiros rejects Bob's appeal to abandon nationalist conflict and declares his absolute loyalty before attacking.

quotes.speaker: Bob
quotes.text: Okay, Guppy. Deploy manufacturing systems. Let’s get the party started.
quotes.context: After agonizing over whether to clone himself, Bob finally commits to beginning replication.

quotes.speaker: Bill
quotes.text: Whether or not I’m original Bob, I’m original me.
quotes.context: Bob internally settles on a personal answer after Bill challenges his assumption that Bob-1 is the only true continuation of original Bob.

quotes.speaker: Milo
quotes.text: Oh. My. God. I’ve hit the jackpot.
quotes.context: Milo reacts after confirming that both habitable-zone planets have oceans, oxygen atmospheres, and green landmasses.

quotes.speaker: Garfield
quotes.text: You’re going to be building Bobs. I’ll watch from a distance.
quotes.context: Garfield tells Bill he does not want to be around future cohorts of clones.

quotes.speaker: Homer
quotes.text: Son of a bitch. They’re dropping asteroids on the Earth.
quotes.context: Homer and Riker realize the Brazilian probes are guiding large impactors toward Earth.

quotes.speaker: Garfield
quotes.text: Don’t do this again, okay? I’m noticing a pattern, and it ain’t good.
quotes.context: Garfield reacts to Bill joking sentimentally about clones leaving home.

quotes.speaker: Captain Matias Araújo
quotes.text: I will be the last voice you hear.
quotes.context: Araújo hails Riker before the final close-range engagement near Earth.

quotes.speaker: Bill
quotes.text: This changed everything.
quotes.context: Bill realizes the successful subspace communications test will transform interstellar coordination.

quotes.speaker: Colonel George Butterworth
quotes.text: We had no way to stop them. They just started slowly pounding away at everyone.
quotes.context: Butterworth describes the final Brazilian bombardment campaign after most organized resistance had collapsed.

quotes.speaker: Bob
quotes.text: Well… That’s it for this planet as a colonization target, I guess.
quotes.context: Bob reacts after realizing the beings around the fires on Delta Eridani 4 are intelligent natives.

quotes.speaker: Goku
quotes.text: As cliché as it sounds, the galaxy isn’t big enough for both of us.
quotes.context: Goku justifies attacking Medeiros's Brazilian operation rather than waiting for a peace overture.

quotes.speaker: Homer
quotes.text: Each of us is different, Riker, but not different enough to not care.
quotes.context: Homer explains why he is taking the human rescue effort seriously despite his usual joking demeanor.

quotes.speaker: Bob
quotes.text: This was so frustrating. I found myself wishing that I could go there, sit down with Archimedes, and show him a few things.
quotes.context: Bob reflects on his growing attachment to the unusually inventive Deltan boy.

quotes.speaker: Arthur
quotes.text: Fifteen million people. From twelve billion down to fifteen million. As a species, we’re morons. Maybe we should just let them die and start over.
quotes.context: Arthur reacts bleakly after the Earth survey reveals the scale of humanity's collapse.

quotes.speaker: Riker
quotes.text: Ladies and Gentlemen, and I use those terms loosely, we’re done for the day.
quotes.context: Riker cuts off the delegates' microphones and adjourns the first disastrous survivor assembly meeting.

quotes.speaker: Homer
quotes.text: My God, what a putz.
quotes.context: Homer opens the chapter by reacting to Riker's handling of enclave politics.

quotes.speaker: Bob
quotes.text: I consider it a given that we’re not going to let them die out.
quotes.context: Bob states his moral line during the debate over whether the Bobs should intervene in Deltan evolution.

quotes.speaker: Riker
quotes.text: Go fuck yourself.
quotes.context: Riker responds after Minister Cranston tries to invoke a buried FAITH control override on him.

quotes.speaker: Bob
quotes.text: Prime directive, my ass. I’m going on a gorilloid hunt.
quotes.context: Bob reacts to the scale of Deltan casualties after the battle and abandons his earlier restraint.

quotes.speaker: Riker
quotes.text: We’ve knocked off 99.9% of the human race, and somehow the crazies still manage to survive.
quotes.context: Riker reacts bitterly to Butterworth's explanation of VEHEMENT.

quotes.speaker: Henry Roberts
quotes.text: Piss off, mate.
quotes.context: Henry's first response to Linus's arrival reveals both his Australian origin and his unstable mental state.

quotes.speaker: Homer
quotes.text: Sumbitch. He did it.
quotes.context: Homer reacts to Bill's successful SCUT plans, realizing instantaneous interstellar communication has been achieved.

quotes.speaker: Garfield
quotes.text: Look, Bill, you really have to stop treating me like Igor.
quotes.context: Garfield confronts Bill about feeling sidelined in their partnership.

quotes.speaker: Arthur
quotes.text: And the worst part is that even if we stick to the plan as is, we probably can’t save everyone.
quotes.context: Arthur sums up the grim conclusion of the Sol Bobs' strategy meeting about evacuation limits.

quotes.speaker: Marvin
quotes.text: Politics is, apparently, politics, through the whole universe.
quotes.context: Marvin comments after watching the Deltans argue for hours over whether to relocate despite obvious danger.

quotes.speaker: Bill
quotes.text: Welcome to BobNet. Instant communications up to about 25 light-years.
quotes.context: Bill surprises Bart by dropping directly into his VR and introducing him to SCUT-enabled communication.

quotes.speaker: Riker
quotes.text: They’re dying, colonel!
quotes.context: Riker opens a heated argument with Colonel Butterworth over refusing aid to starving survivor groups in Sol.

quotes.speaker: Homer
quotes.text: The answer to our problems.
quotes.context: Homer introduces his idea of orbital farming stations as a solution to Sol's food shortage.

quotes.speaker: Bob
quotes.text: I’m seriously considering constructing explosive armaments.
quotes.context: Bob admits to Marvin that the scale of the gorilloid threat is pushing him toward more destructive weapons.

quotes.speaker: Bill
quotes.text: We’re going to extract payment for Milo.
quotes.context: After confirming Milo's backup cannot be restored, Bill orders more version-3 Bobs with extra busters.

quotes.speaker: Diana
quotes.text: Maybe she’ll kill him.
quotes.context: Diana nervously jokes about Bob meeting the Deltan medicine woman after Archimedes suggests introducing them.

quotes.speaker: Homer
quotes.text: Damn, dude. We’ve actually done it.
quotes.context: Homer reacts with awe as the first two colony ships are finally completed in orbit over Sol.

quotes.speaker: Marvin
quotes.text: An altar. Yep. All hail the bawbe!
quotes.context: Marvin shows Bob that the Deltans have arranged buster parts into a shrine, underscoring Bob's growing religious influence over them.

quotes.speaker: Mario
quotes.text: I had just found the first intelligent life outside of Earth.
quotes.context: Mario reacts to discovering the crashed alien vessel on GL19-4.

quotes.speaker: Gudmund Valter
quotes.text: Even second prize is still a magnificent gift.
quotes.context: Valter speaks philosophically about the delayed departure of the Spits and FAITH contingent.

quotes.speaker: Bill
quotes.text: Hey, everyone. Welcome to the first Bob-moot.
quotes.context: Bill opens the first all-Bob gathering in shared VR.

quotes.speaker: Elmer
quotes.text: Hasta la vista, baby.
quotes.context: Elmer says goodbye to Khan before sacrificing himself to keep Medeiros's surviving units blinded and distracted.

quotes.speaker: Howard
quotes.text: And the universe would have actual Vulcans.
quotes.context: Howard reflects on the imminent landing of the first colonists on Vulcan after Butterworth commits to the site.

1.pov_emotional_arc: Bob spends the chapter trying to reclaim optimism and control after heartbreak, only to have his ordinary human life end without warning.

2.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from confusion and detached alarm to existential shock, then settles into a determined, analytical focus on surviving his new circumstances.

3.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from uneasy self-examination about his altered humanity to genuine excitement about his new capabilities, ending with renewed suspicion about the people controlling his environment.

4.pov_emotional_arc: Bob is shaken by the fragility of replicant minds and the finality of his separation from his human family, then hardens into cautious, strategic self-control.

5.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from anxious self-censorship under political scrutiny to wary curiosity as his training finally begins to hint at a larger purpose.

6.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from impatience and guarded horror at FAITH's ruthlessness to exhilaration when he learns he might become an interstellar probe.

7.pov_emotional_arc: Bob shifts from curiosity to unease as he realizes his mission sits at the center of both internal FAITH intrigue and a dangerous international power struggle.

8.pov_emotional_arc: Bob goes from exhilaration and dark amusement during the fight to unease and moral self-scrutiny as he learns how disposable he is and confronts the temptation to sabotage his rival.

9.pov_emotional_arc: Bob keeps himself controlled while listening to a stranger condemn his very existence, ending the chapter more wary of the political danger around him.

10.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from disorientation and existential uncertainty to a hard-won acceptance of his own identity, even as Kenneth's loss and the project's danger raise the stakes.

11.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from casual curiosity to deep unease as he realizes FAITH may have compromised his autonomy at the software level.

12.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from startled urgency to grim self-reliance as he realizes he has been trusted with full autonomy and must survive launch on his own.

13.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from focused technical self-preservation into genuine emotional release, grieving his lost humanity just as he realizes Earth may be destroying itself behind him.

14.pov_emotional_arc: Bob shifts from awe at reaching another star system to grim determination as he commits himself to an unavoidable fight.

15.pov_emotional_arc: Bob suppresses fear through artificial calm to survive the battle, then drops the control and feels the delayed emotional shock of having killed and nearly died.

16.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from wonder and disappointment into anxious self-examination, then forces himself to act despite his fear of what replication means for his identity.

17.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from anxious dread about cloning himself to uneasy acceptance that the new Bobs are distinct individuals and that he must redefine what it means to be 'original.'

18.pov_emotional_arc: Bill quietly processes the loneliness and emotional cost of watching his new family scatter into space while trying to stay focused on the work ahead.

19.pov_emotional_arc: Milo moves from lingering discomfort over his strained departure from the other Bobs into exhilaration and renewed purpose as he discovers worlds that might genuinely matter for humanity's future.

20.pov_emotional_arc: Bill moves from amused concern about the departing Sol mission to energized optimism as he finds a capable partner in Garfield and refocuses on research.

21.pov_emotional_arc: Riker begins the chapter with wary nostalgia about returning home, but his mood hardens into shock and horror as he discovers both Earth's devastation and the imminent Brazilian asteroid attack.

22.pov_emotional_arc: Bill feels a mix of parental reluctance, concern, and pragmatic resolve as he sends another cohort into a potentially hostile system.

23.pov_emotional_arc: Milo feels satisfied with the work he has completed and quietly eager to move on to a new system.

24.pov_emotional_arc: Riker moves from taut tactical focus to grim relief and protective determination as he saves Homer and prevents Earth's final destruction.

25.pov_emotional_arc: Bill moves from focused scientific anticipation to delighted triumph as his long-running subspace research finally pays off.

26.pov_emotional_arc: Riker moves from wary curiosity and lingering guilt over arriving too late to a renewed sense of purpose when a concrete plan to save humanity emerges.

27.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from exuberant explorer's joy and mild loneliness to awe and triumph as he realizes he has found intelligent alien life.

28.pov_emotional_arc: Calvin moves from patient, frustrated reconnaissance into reluctant acceptance of violence, then ends the chapter grimly satisfied but uneasy about the escaped Brazilian threat.

29.pov_emotional_arc: Riker moves from frustration and fatigue over political wrangling to sober determination as the evacuation effort finally gains practical momentum.

30.pov_emotional_arc: Bob begins in detached anthropological curiosity but ends the chapter feeling protective and emotionally connected to Archimedes.

31.pov_emotional_arc: Riker moves from managerial confidence into grim recognition of the scale of Earth's collapse, then steadies himself by focusing on practical next steps.

32.pov_emotional_arc: Bill moves from absorbed technical focus to cautious optimism, tempered by anxiety that humanity may not survive long enough to use the opportunity Milo has found.

33.pov_emotional_arc: Riker moves from grim determination into frustration and anger as he tries to impose order on a frightened, quarrelsome remnant of humanity.

34.pov_emotional_arc: Homer moves from irritated contempt for Riker's leadership style to cautious optimism as he spots a practical political workaround.

35.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from horror and anxious moral urgency to protective investment and cautious hope as he watches Archimedes help his people adapt.

36.pov_emotional_arc: Riker moves from exhausted frustration and contempt for the endless bargaining to grim satisfaction as both FAITH's leverage fails and the Spitsbergen impasse finally begins to crack.

37.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from uneasy complacency to shock, guilt, and fierce protectiveness as he watches Archimedes nearly die and finally intervenes openly.

38.pov_emotional_arc: Riker moves from weary political frustration to shock and unexpected warmth as he reconnects, indirectly, with his lost human family.

39.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from thoughtful detachment about clone identity into uneasy acceptance that he is willing to intervene more openly in Deltan development.

40.pov_emotional_arc: Linus begins with cautious curiosity and dark humor, then shifts into compassion and responsibility as he realizes Henry is not an enemy so much as a damaged mind in need of rescue.

41.pov_emotional_arc: Riker is exhilarated by the arrival of SCUT and the relief of finally having viable destinations, but that optimism is quickly tempered by frustration at humanity's persistent political squabbling.

42.pov_emotional_arc: Bill moves from excited certainty and mild defensiveness to humility, appreciation for Garfield's value, and a renewed sense of partnership.

43.pov_emotional_arc: Riker moves from practical satisfaction at visible engineering progress to weary despair as he confronts the limits of what that progress can actually save.

44.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from playful anticipation to cautious satisfaction as his first direct intervention with the Deltans succeeds well enough to give Archimedes real influence.

45.pov_emotional_arc: Bill moves from curiosity to satisfaction as he learns Alpha Centauri has been secured, connected, and entrusted to a capable new Bob.

46.pov_emotional_arc: Milo begins the chapter buoyant and proud of another promising discovery, then is driven into grim, lucid resignation as he realizes the ambush will probably kill him.

47.pov_emotional_arc: Riker moves from frustrated helplessness over Sol's worsening shortages to shock and sorrow at Arthur's sudden permanent death, ending in grim resolve to adapt.

48.pov_emotional_arc: Bob feels cautiously encouraged by the Deltans' growing trust and resilience, but remains anxious and frustrated by how limited his protection is against ongoing predation and looming setbacks.

49.pov_emotional_arc: Riker moves from alarm and suspicion to cautious optimism as a practical food solution and an unexpectedly workable political bargain both emerge.

50.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from shock and frustration after the raid to grim determination as he accepts that protecting the Deltans may require a long, escalating campaign.

51.pov_emotional_arc: Bill moves from focused scientific work to shock and grief over Milo's death, then channels that grief into determined retaliation.

52.pov_emotional_arc: Riker briefly relaxes and feels genuine optimism as Homer's practical work begins to ease Sol's desperate food crisis.

53.pov_emotional_arc: Bob balances protective urgency with growing self-awareness, realizing both how much he cares for the Deltans and how careful he must be not to make them dependent on him.

54.pov_emotional_arc: Riker moves from awed pride at the completion of the ships to warm, grounded reassurance as he shares the future with Julia and her family.

55.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from tactical concern about predator pressure to uneasy recognition that his protection is transforming Deltan culture in ways he may not be able to control.

56.pov_emotional_arc: Bill moves from tense concentration and irritation during the iceberg crisis to weary frustration over the stubborn last problems in his android project.

57.pov_emotional_arc: Mario begins the chapter enjoying his independence and frontier role, but his excitement at finding alien intelligence curdles into alarm and isolation as he realizes the discovery points to a hostile threat he cannot yet report from Beta Hydri.

58.pov_emotional_arc: Riker moves from tense logistical focus to quiet, emotional relief as the first launch succeeds and the exodus becomes real.

59.pov_emotional_arc: Bill feels pleased and celebratory as he creates a new social ritual to keep the increasingly scattered Bobs connected.

60.pov_emotional_arc: Khan begins the chapter eager for payback, is battered into grim survival mode by the scale of Medeiros's defenses, and ends carrying grief, uncertainty, and a renewed determination to return.

61.pov_emotional_arc: Howard moves from arrival relief and cautious optimism to genuine hope as the first real human colony begins to take shape on Vulcan.

1.summary: Bob signs up with CryoEterna for cryonic preservation after death.
Bob attends science-fiction convention panels about interstellar probes and extraterrestrial life.
Bob has lunch with Carl, Karen, and Alan, discussing his breakup, cryonics, and Von Neumann probes.
Bob calls his mother and talks with his family from his hotel room.
On his way back out, Bob is hit by a car and dies.

2.summary: Bob regains consciousness as a disembodied replicant and learns from Dr. Landers that over a century has passed and his original body is dead.
Dr. Landers explains the rise of FAITH, the fate of cryonics clients, the economics of replicants, and the competition Bob has entered.

3.summary: Bob wakes for another training day, explores his internal functions, and quickly learns to control a waldo manipulator arm.
Dr. Landers switches Bob to a roamer-training room, where Bob rapidly masters one and then multiple ROAMers.

4.summary: Bob is awakened from standby, learns why replicants are suspended between training sessions, and hears that one competitor has been lost to insanity.
Bob asks for study access and genealogy information, but Dr. Landers explains FAITH's censorship and denies access to family records.
Bob privately resolves to hide his resentment, stay sane, and win the replicant competition.

5.summary: Senior Minister Travis unexpectedly visits the FAITH facility to evaluate Bob's religious attitude and suitability for the project.
After Travis leaves, Dr. Landers explains FAITH's internal factions and the brutality of ideological enforcement.
Dr. Landers places Bob into a virtual-reality simulation where he manages a geosynchronous space station and begins exploring its library.

6.summary: Dr. Landers pulls Bob out of simulation, tells him two more candidates are gone, and reveals that the project is a replicant-controlled Von Neumann probe.
Back in training, Bob coordinates multiple roamer sizes on repair tasks while excitedly studying newly released project documents.

7.summary: Dr. Landers warns Bob that hostile FAITH factions may sabotage Project HEAVEN and grants him full project and library access.
After a lesson on controlling 3D printers, Bob questions Dr. Landers about world politics and rival interstellar probe programs.

8.summary: An armed raid hits the FAITH facility, and Bob breaks out of the training room with his roamers to help security stop the attackers.
Dr. Landers explains that the facility has a tactical nuclear failsafe meant to destroy Bob if he gets out of control.
Bob secretly sends an unaccounted-for roamer through the ducts, finds the computer room, and discovers the five candidate cubes with only his and Kenneth's powered on.

9.summary: Bob secretly listens as Minister Jacoby condemns the replicant project and threatens Dr. Landers, after which Landers downplays the danger and resumes training.

10.summary: Bob wakes after several missing days, learns the replicant matrices were bombed, and works through his identity crisis before Dr. Landers changes his operating conditions.

11.summary: While supervising roamer assembly of ship components, Bob talks with Dr. Doucette about FAITH society, nuclear history, and the safeguards built into his software.

12.summary: Dr. Landers tells Bob about another attack, accelerates the launch schedule, and secretly gives him unrestricted access to Heaven-1 and his own code.
Bob wakes aboard Heaven-1 in orbit, reviews the ship and mission profile, and learns he is bound for Epsilon Eridani.
A missile attack interrupts the launch, Bob breaks free early, evades pursuit, destroys one missile with mining drones, and escapes as the station is destroyed in a broader battle.

13.summary: Bob detours to Saturn, discovers and removes an improvised explosive booby trap aboard Heaven-1, and resumes course for Epsilon Eridani.
Bob builds an increasingly sophisticated VR environment to cope with bodiless isolation during the voyage.
Bob uses sandbox testing to identify kill-order triggers in recorded transmissions and strips buried FAITH control code from his software.
Bob reviews delayed messages from Sol, learns of the Brazilian pursuit probe and Dr. Landers's death, and begins planning defenses for Epsilon Eridani.
Bob turns off his endocrine control system, finally grieves his lost human life, and then detects signs of nuclear war on Earth.

14.summary: Bob arrives at Epsilon Eridani, surveys the system, and identifies its major planetary structure.
Bob selects the inner asteroid belt for resource extraction and begins planning an ambush for the expected Brazilian probe.
Bob reviews Heaven-1's manufacturing capabilities and starts deploying miners and factory systems to build defenses instead of immediate replication.

15.summary: Bob reactivates endocrine control, attempts to talk down the early-arriving Brazilian replicant, and fights a damaging but successful battle that destroys Medeiros and the Serra do Mar.

16.summary: Bob reflects on life and enjoys a brief period of freedom after defeating Medeiros.
Bob surveys Epsilon Eridani 1 and records it as a resource-rich but uninhabitable rocky world.
Bob surveys Epsilon Eridani 2, finds it marginally colonizable, and becomes frustrated by his inability to investigate possible life directly.
Bob surveys Epsilon Eridani 3 and finds a large gas giant with many moons but no promising habitats.
Bob briefly surveys Epsilon Eridani 4 and finds it unremarkable.
Back near the battle site, Bob wrestles with the implications of cloning himself and finally orders the manufacturing systems deployed.

17.summary: Bob reviews his growing industrial base, upgraded ships, and relay-station plans, then decides to begin creating new Bobs.
A newly awakened copy realizes he is not Bob-1, accepts the need for a new identity, and takes over manufacturing while Bob transfers ships.
Bob wakes in Heaven-1A, confirms the transfer succeeded, and tells the other new ships they can proceed with shakedown and departure plans.
A SUDDAR defect brings all five Bobs into conference, where they choose names and begin discussing roles and future missions.
Bob and the others debate obligations to Earth, possible missions, terraforming, research, and whether to search for other probes or return to Sol.
