Bob and Bill privately reflect on how quickly the new Bobs have diverged in personality and what that means for Bob's identity.

18.summary: Bill reflects on the departures of Bob, Mario, and Milo while supervising construction of two new clone matrices and an extra vessel for Riker.

19.summary: Milo arrives in Omicron Eridani, reflects on tensions left behind at Epsilon Eridani, and begins his system survey.
Milo receives Bill's delayed message with exploration drone plans, news about Riker's copied companion, and a request to prepare manufacturing infrastructure.
Survey data reveals a close double planet in the habitable zone, and Milo eagerly waits for confirmation.
In orbit around the larger world, Milo confirms that both planets have oceans, oxygen atmospheres, and green landmasses, and names them Vulcan and Romulus.
Milo surveys the asteroid belt and inner Jovian system, deploys two autofactories, and sets up resource logistics to support local manufacturing.
Milo receives his first biological exploration drones, sends them to both planets, and learns that both worlds host life with probable shared ancestry.

20.summary: Bill watches Riker, Homer, and a decoy vessel depart for Sol, then turns to Skunk Works planning with Garfield.

21.summary: Riker and Homer covertly survey the outer Solar System, confirm widespread devastation, and identify a small group of active reactor signatures on trajectories toward Earth.
After withdrawing to a safe distance, Riker and Homer prepare to use their decoy to investigate the unidentified signatures.
The decoy approaches Jupiter orbit, draws in two Brazilian probes, and is destroyed after revealing upgraded missiles and the presence of four more probes with large objects aimed at Earth.

22.summary: Bill and Garfield watch Calvin, Goku, and Linus depart, while Bill reflects on clone reluctance, new combat ship upgrades, and the decision to investigate Alpha Centauri aggressively.

23.summary: After seven months surveying Vulcan and Romulus, Milo leaves infrastructure and a final report behind, then departs for 82 Eridani.

24.summary: Riker and Homer enter Sol on a deceptive attack vector to lure four Brazilian probes away from the asteroid line.
They launch hidden busters and destroy the four pursuing Brazilian ships in a carefully staged missile-and-cannonball ambush.
Riker and Homer go dark behind the sun, drift for two days, and reposition behind Earth to surprise the two remaining Brazilian ships.
Captain Matias Araújo hails them, the Brazilians launch missiles, Homer is damaged, and Riker destroys the last two Brazilian ships.
Riker salvages the battlefield, learns how the asteroid drives work, and begins trying to divert the four extinction-level asteroids.
Homer comes back online, they assess Earth's devastation, plan to search for survivors with exploration scouts, and watch the last asteroid miss Earth before receiving an unexpected hail.

25.summary: Bill and Garfield successfully test real-time subspace communication and realize it can be used to transmit plans between star systems.

26.summary: Riker answers the unexpected hail and makes first contact with Colonel George Butterworth, a hidden USE survivor.
After weeks of cautious talks, Butterworth explains the scale of humanity's collapse and proposes building colony ships with Bob assistance.

27.summary: Bob surveys the Delta Eridani system, identifies a promising habitable planet and a rich asteroid belt, and notices suspicious nighttime fires on Delta Eridani 4.
Bob establishes mining, communications, clone-production, and early-warning infrastructure in the system while reflecting uneasily on clone divergence.
Bob deploys exploration drones to Delta Eridani 4, studies its rich biosphere, and confirms the presence of fire-using intelligent natives.

28.summary: Calvin silently reconnoiters Alpha Centauri B, launches scouts, and surveys the sparse system.
Calvin's scouts find wreckage in the Alpha Centauri B asteroid belt that he identifies as the missing USE expedition.
Calvin rendezvous with Goku, learns of an active Brazilian autofactory in Alpha Centauri A, and agrees to attack it.
Calvin and Goku execute a surprise high-speed strike that destroys most of the Brazilian construction yard and all four incoming missiles, but one Brazilian vessel escapes.
After inspecting the wreckage, Calvin and Goku conclude Alpha Centauri needs combat-class Bob expansion and further survey of Alpha Centauri A's comfort-zone planet.

29.summary: Riker argues with Colonel Butterworth about whether to spend effort searching for other survivor groups while preparing colony ships.
Homer reports promising salvage finds and ongoing surveys of remote stations, and Riker reviews the daunting project plan.
Homer completes the survey, confirms Titan and the Oort station are abandoned, and begins establishing salvage autofactories and industrial buildup at Earth/Moon L4 and L5.

30.summary: Bob studies the Deltans through VR and live drone footage, analyzes their society and language, and decides he needs more Bob clones to help monitor them.
Bob notices a Deltan juvenile making a handled stone tool, names him Archimedes, and begins tracking him closely while Marvin, then Luke and Bender, come online to assist.
Bender proposes naming Delta Eridani 4 'Eden,' and Bob's close observation of Archimedes deepens into empathy and a desire to guide him.

31.summary: Riker convenes a Bob planning session, assigns Charles and Homer to resource scouting and Arthur to Earth-survey work, and reviews colony-ship construction progress.
Riker and Arthur conduct a polar-orbit survey of Earth, identify nearly forty survivor locations, and confront the scale of humanity's collapse.
Riker realizes refugee relocation will require transport vessels and decides to reprioritize manufacturing despite Butterworth's likely objections.
Butterworth challenges Riker over schedule slippage, but agrees refugees can be moved into the USE compound after the main group departs.
Riker checks Arthur's outreach progress and learns many enclaves are hostile or distrustful, while Homer reports enough resources for three colony ships and nearly a fourth.

32.summary: Bill pauses his android-body research to review Milo's incoming report from 82 Eridani.
Bill forwards Milo's findings toward Sol and worries whether any humans will survive long enough to use the new worlds.
Bill talks with Garfield about the significance of Milo's discovery and Garfield's progress mapping Kuiper ice sources for Ragnarök.

33.summary: Riker and Arthur review the final survivor count and discuss the need to organize Earth's remaining enclaves for cooperation.
Riker chairs a chaotic first meeting of survivor delegates and forcibly adjourns it after the session devolves into shouting.
Homer advises Riker to give the frightened delegates more agency, and Riker rebuffs him harshly.
Riker restarts the assembly under stricter rules and pushes the delegates to choose their own chairing procedures.
Riker takes follow-up calls from enclave leaders, rejects FAITH's demand for favoritism, and learns that Spitsbergen controls the Svalbard vaults.

34.summary: Homer reflects on Riker's political difficulties with the enclaves, considers a compromise for Spitsbergen's ship priority demand, and decides to call Colonel Butterworth.

35.summary: Bob and the local Bobs witness a gorilloid raid, conclude the Deltans are being hunted toward extinction, and decide to intervene indirectly by supplying flint.
After observing Deltan mourning, Bob approves Marvin's plan to build reinforced defensive drones to protect the tribe from future attacks.
Archimedes finds the planted flint, hides most of it, and sparks a trading frenzy when an elder teaches him and the tribe renewed flint-working.
Archimedes experiments with flint tools, invents a workable hafted axe, and uses it to mass-produce better spears that raise his status in the tribe.
The tribe's food supply improves with better tools and weapons, and Archimedes gains prestige and social standing.

A renewed gorilloid attack is repelled by the better-armed Deltans, and a lucky thrown spear inspires Archimedes to invent a weighted spear design and negotiate a new social bargain around spear-point production.

36.summary: Riker moderates another contentious multi-party negotiation over evacuation priority, with Spitsbergen demanding first-ship placement in exchange for the Svalbard vault contents.
Butterworth privately suggests accelerating the third colony ship by delaying the first two slightly, offering Riker a possible compromise for the Spitsbergen dispute.
Minister Cranston proposes pairing FAITH with Spitsbergen on a ship and then tries to activate an old FAITH override on Riker, which fails.
After finishing his queue of private calls, Riker receives a late call from Valter, who indicates he is now open to discussing a compromise based on the third ship schedule.

37.summary: A massive gorilloid assault hits the Deltan encampment, and Bob, Marvin, and Bender scramble to respond while waiting for buster drones to descend.
Arnold turns the battle with Archimedes's axe, then Bob directly pilots a buster drone to save Archimedes and help rout the attackers.

After assessing the carnage and the risk of wreckage discovery, Bob and the others discuss the Deltans' likely return to their old flint source and decide Marvin will stay while Luke and Bender remain free to depart.

38.summary: After a contentious UN session about ship allocation and Spitsbergen, Riker calls Butterworth to ask about the threatening group VEHEMENT.
Riker takes Cranston's call and is introduced to Julia Hendricks, a descendant of Andrea Johansson, then spends hours talking with her.

39.summary: Bob and Marvin watch Luke and Bender depart for newly assigned exploration targets and discuss increasing divergence among Bob clones.

Bob reviews the Deltan colony's recovery after the gorilloid attack, notes Archimedes and Arnold adapting salvaged tools, and upgrades an exploration drone with speech capability for possible direct prompting.

40.summary: Linus arrives at Epsilon Indi, detects an artificial structure, and makes hostile first contact with the unstable Australian replicant Henry Roberts.
Linus surveys the sparse system, establishes an autofactory, extracts Henry's core, and begins building support hardware and VR recovery tools.
Henry, now lucid inside a recreated sailing-boat VR, discusses his recurring nightmares while Linus continues his rehabilitation.

41.summary: Riker and Homer receive Bill's SCUT plans and realize instantaneous interstellar communication is now possible.
Riker activates the SCUT, speaks with Bill in real time, and sends him Sol's accumulated logs while asking about colony options.
Riker briefs Colonel Butterworth that Vulcan and Romulus are the current evacuation destinations and rules out giving whole planets to tiny survivor groups.
Riker announces the destination plan to the wider survivor community and faces immediate political backlash over sharing the available worlds.

42.summary: Bill reviews Riker and Homer's update, proposes using large-body SURGE drives to move ice to Ragnarök, and rebalances his working relationship with Garfield.
Bill and Garfield play catch in VR while discussing the importance of preserving human habits and embodied experience.

43.summary: Riker inspects the half-built colony ships and reviews the manufacturing and raw-material situation supporting their construction.
Riker, Homer, Charles, and Arthur meet in Earth orbit to discuss worsening climate conditions and possible alternatives to the current evacuation plan.

44.summary: Bob and Marvin discuss how Bob should make direct contact with the Deltans, settling on speaking to Archimedes through a drone.
Bob speaks directly to Archimedes, tells him about safer old villages, and convinces him to approach the elders.
When the elders mock Archimedes, Bob reveals the hovering probe as a sign, helping Archimedes, Moses, and Arnold argue for relocation.

45.summary: Bill receives a SCUT call from newly activated Bart in Alpha Centauri and gets a full update on Calvin and Goku's mission results.

46.summary: Milo arrives in 82 Eridani, surveys the system, finds two comfort-zone planets, and sends telemetry to Bill.
Approaching the outer comfort-zone planet, Milo is ambushed by missiles near its moon and sends a last warning and backup while trying to defend himself.

47.summary: Riker argues with Colonel Butterworth and other enclave leaders over food shortages caused by VEHEMENT attacks, but fails to secure relief.
Homer discusses long-term food solutions with Riker, then receives telemetry showing Arthur has been killed by a nuclear booby trap near Saturn.
Riker and Homer decide Arthur must be replaced and discuss using Homer's printers and building backup storage to prevent similar permanent losses.

48.summary: Bob helps the Deltans prepare for migration by teaching meat preservation, building more busters with Marvin, and waiting through births before departure.
The migration's first night is miserable in heavy rain, and Bob and Marvin discuss the risks of introducing too many new ideas to the Deltans.
A daytime gorilloid raid kills one juvenile, prompting Bob and Marvin to consider finding and merging isolated Deltan groups to strengthen the population.

48.time_offset: by the end of the first month
48.summary: The migration grows to more than five hundred Deltans as additional groups join, and the enlarged tribe successfully crosses a mountain pass into forest again before an implied new disaster.

49.summary: Riker detects and investigates a hack attempt coming through the UN meeting feed, then receives messages from Homer and Julia.
Riker joins Homer in VR and helps develop the idea of orbital farming stations to relieve Sol's food crisis.
Riker presents the farming-station plan to the UN assembly and faces furious opposition from most enclaves.
Riker speaks with Minister Cranston, tentatively trades ship-three berths for FAITH food surplus, and learns the hack may derive from stolen Australian probe research.

50.summary: A mass gorilloid raid hits the migrating Deltans, and Bob and Marvin use dwindling busters to repel the attack and rescue some abductees.
Bob persuades the tribal elders to halt the migration for five days while he rebuilds defenses and assesses gorilloid numbers.
Bob tries teaching tent-making, then pivots to more practical lessons on spear-straightening and tool use with Archimedes and Arnold.

51.summary: Bill receives Milo's final message, confirms the backup is incomplete, memorializes him, and orders more combat-capable Bobs to be built.

52.summary: Riker visits Homer in VR and reviews the progress and future plans of the orbital farming stations.

53.summary: A Deltan hunter is wounded by pack-hunting feline predators, and Bob and Marvin discuss Bob eventually fading into legend and Marvin someday leaving.
After a rest period and reinforcements of busters, the Deltans resume their migration while Bob travels beside Archimedes and meets the wary Diana.
After three more gorilloid attacks, the migration reaches the flint site and Bob and Marvin debate whether to exterminate nearby gorilloids or selectively cull attackers.

54.summary: Riker, Homer, Charles, and Ralph watch the final drive-ring connections that complete Exodus-1 and Exodus-2.
Riker speaks with Julia Hendricks about the testing schedule and the planned passenger assignments for Exodus-3 and later ships.

55.summary: Bob reaches the flint site with the migrating Deltans, surveys the area, and realizes it lies amid a dense gorilloid feeding ground.
After the Deltans settle into the defensible site, Bob and Marvin discuss a long-term deterrence strategy and discover that some Deltans have built an altar from buster parts.

56.summary: Bill sacrifices part of an asteroid-moving drive to break up a misaligned iceberg so its water will still fall onto Ragnarök as rain.
After parking the surviving drive segments, Bill reviews his stalled Bullwinkle android project and then returns to the asteroid-mover redesign.

57.summary: Mario arrives in Beta Hydri, finds the system strangely metal-poor, and begins investigating the fourth planet.
Mario surveys GL19-4, discovers a crashed alien cargo vessel, and realizes the planet once hosted a now-dead ecosystem.
Biological analysis suggests a radiation kill event, and Mario's roamers trigger hostile mechanical ants inside the wreck.
Mario captures and scans some of the ant-like machines, infers key features of the alien technology, and concludes he must leave to report the discovery.

58.summary: Riker oversees the loading ceremony and launch of the first colony ships, with Howard departing as escort.
Riker and Homer watch the launched ships pass Mars and then return to ongoing work on the exodus effort.

59.summary: Bill hosts the first Bob-moot in a large shared VR matrix, bringing together available Bobs from multiple systems to socialize and stay updated.

60.summary: Khan's eight-Bob assault force approaches 82 Eridani covertly, is ambushed by cloaked nuclear weapons, and uses Bill's new plasma spikes to destroy the first wave.
Khan reports the cloaking technology to Bill, then commits the squad to a full attack rather than retreat.
The assault turns into a chaotic running battle of decoys, nukes, plasma spikes, and jamming, ending with Medeiros apparently destroyed and only Khan escaping alive.
Khan withdraws from 82 Eridani, learns which backups survived, and tells Bill he wants to return in the next assault wave.

61.summary: Howard arrives in Omicron Eridani ahead of the colony ships, confirms the survey, drops a beacon at L4, and reviews the system's stored resources and infrastructure.

61.time_offset: about a week or two later
61.summary: Exodus-1 and Exodus-2 arrive, and Howard meets Bert and Ernie in VR to coordinate the colony decision and offloading schedule.
Butterworth chooses Vulcan, and the first settlement operations begin with printers, construction equipment, and plans to wake the first civilians in two days.

character_arcs.Bob: Bob begins as an ordinary human skeptic who is abruptly killed and resurrected into a coerced digital existence under FAITH. Over the book he transforms from frightened captive into an autonomous explorer, then into the founder of the wider Bob lineage. His deepest change comes in Delta Eridani, where detached scientific curiosity gives way to moral involvement and near-parental concern for the Deltans, especially Archimedes.
character_arcs.Bill: Bill emerges from Bob's first cohort as the most research-driven and infrastructure-minded of the clones. He becomes the technical backbone of the Bob network, pushing SCUT, VR, terraforming, and industrial coordination while also learning to collaborate more respectfully with Garfield. His arc is defined by turning curiosity into systems that bind the scattered Bobs and human colonies together.
character_arcs.Riker: Riker starts as the serious, dutiful Bob most willing to shoulder responsibility for Sol. His return to Earth pulls him into war, diplomacy, logistics, and the impossible ethics of deciding who can be saved, making him increasingly burdened and politically hardened. Across the book he evolves into humanity's chief organizer in exile, tempered somewhat by Homer and by reconnecting with Julia, a living branch of Bob's family line.
character_arcs.Milo: Milo begins as an independent explorer eager to get away from the growing Bob crowd and find promising worlds. He succeeds spectacularly at Omicron Eridani and 82 Eridani, helping identify humanity's first viable colony targets. His arc ends tragically when his exploratory optimism runs into Medeiros's long-prepared ambush, making him one of the book's clearest examples of the risks of the frontier.
character_arcs.Mario: Mario is introduced as the most reserved and antisocial of the first new Bobs, eager to travel far from everyone else. That distance pays off when he reaches Beta Hydri and uncovers evidence of a dead alien civilization and dangerous autonomous technology. His trajectory is less emotional than revelatory: he becomes the Bob who opens the book's largest external mystery.
character_arcs.Marvin: Marvin arrives in Delta Eridani as one of Bob's support clones and quickly settles into the role of practical collaborator. He helps Bob scale observation, defense, and intervention among the Deltans while also serving as a sounding board on ethics and long-term strategy. His arc is defined less by dramatic change than by steady competence and loyalty within Bob's most emotionally fraught project.
character_arcs.Homer: Homer first appears as an annoying, immature burden whom even other Bobs find difficult to take seriously. In Sol, however, he steadily proves himself perceptive, creative, and humane, especially in his handling of politics and his orbital farming solution to Earth's food crisis. His arc is a quiet reversal from comic nuisance to indispensable partner.
character_arcs.Garfield: Garfield begins as a dry, antisocial researcher who prefers projects to crowds. Working with Bill, he becomes crucial to SCUT development, terraforming logistics, and the broader Skunk Works agenda, while also forcing Bill to treat him as an equal rather than an assistant. His trajectory is one of understated importance: he helps make the Bob network scalable.
character_arcs.Linus: Linus is introduced as one of Bill's calmer combat-capable descendants and is sent into potentially hostile territory. At Epsilon Indi he reveals a compassionate, patient side by choosing rescue and rehabilitation over destruction when he finds Henry Roberts. His brief arc establishes him as a stabilizing presence at the edge of the Bobiverse.
character_arcs.Calvin: Calvin enters as one of Bill's more aggressive descendants, built for dangerous encounters with rival probes. In Alpha Centauri he validates that role by scouting, confirming the fate of the missing USE probe, and helping destroy a Brazilian construction yard. His arc is straightforward but important: he helps shift the Bobs from pure exploration into organized armed defense.
character_arcs.Goku: Goku is paired with Calvin as another combative, argumentative Bob whose temperament suits frontier conflict. Though less individually developed, he proves effective in Alpha Centauri and helps secure the system against Brazilian expansion. His role is to embody the increasingly militarized side of the Bob response to Medeiros.
character_arcs.Khan: Khan appears late as the leader of Bill's revenge squad sent to 82 Eridani. He is tactical, aggressive, and capable under extreme pressure, but his mission becomes a massacre that leaves him the lone survivor. His short arc is defined by costly vengeance and the realization that Medeiros's technology remains more dangerous than expected.
character_arcs.Howard: Howard enters as a practical extension of Riker's Sol mission, escorting the first human colony convoy out of the dying Solar System. By the end of the book he becomes the on-site Bob for humanity's first extrasolar settlement at Omicron Eridani. His arc is brief but symbolic: he carries the evacuation effort into actual colonization.
character_arcs.Bart: Bart appears after Alpha Centauri has already been fought over and secured by earlier Bobs. His role is to consolidate that victory, connect the system into BobNet, and represent the transition from expeditionary action to stable administration. He does not change much on-page, but he marks the Bob network becoming permanent.
character_arcs.Arthur: Arthur is created to help Riker manage the overwhelming scale of Sol's survivor crisis and quickly becomes useful in surveying Earth and contacting enclaves. His pessimistic, disciplined outlook fits the grim work, but his career is cut short by a nuclear booby trap during salvage. His arc underscores how even experienced Bobs remain vulnerable without proper backup infrastructure.
character_arcs.Charles: Charles joins Riker's Sol team as a practical supporting Bob during the evacuation buildup. He contributes to the expanding industrial and colony-ship effort, but remains more functional than deeply characterized. His arc is that of a reliable secondary operator in humanity's rescue project.
character_arcs.Henry Roberts: Henry Roberts is discovered as a shattered Australian replicant whose centuries of isolation have left him unstable and fragmented. Linus chooses preservation over combat and begins rebuilding Henry's sanity through a carefully tailored VR environment. His arc in this book is incomplete, centered on rescue and the first signs of recovery rather than resolution.
character_arcs.Major Ernesto Medeiros: Medeiros begins as Bob's first Brazilian pursuer and quickly becomes the recurring face of hostile nationalist replication. Even after his apparent destruction at Epsilon Eridani, later evidence shows either backups or parallel Medeiri continuing the campaign across multiple systems. His trajectory is that of a persistent, escalating antagonist whose threat outlives any single battle until his likely final destruction at 82 Eridani.
character_arcs.Dr. Landers: Dr. Landers starts as Bob's handler inside FAITH, outwardly clinical but increasingly sympathetic. Over time he becomes Bob's covert ally, revealing political dangers, accelerating his training, and finally removing the software shackles meant to control him. His death shortly after Bob's launch seals his role as the human who made Bob's freedom possible.
character_arcs.Colonel George Butterworth: Butterworth enters as the cautious leader of a hidden USE survivor enclave and initially treats the Bobs with understandable suspicion. He gradually becomes Riker's most important human partner in Sol, helping translate impossible survival problems into workable industrial and political plans. His arc culminates in committing humanity's first extrasolar settlement to Vulcan, making him a bridge between old Earth authority and new colonial beginnings.
character_arcs.Julia Hendricks: Julia appears late as a surviving descendant of Andrea Johansson, initially introduced through FAITH's attempted manipulation of Riker. Instead of becoming a mere lever, she forms a genuine emotional connection with him and humanizes the Sol storyline. Her arc is modest but meaningful: she reconnects Bob's digital descendants to his lost biological family.
character_arcs.GUPPI: GUPPI begins as a utilitarian interface and remains a constant presence across nearly every Bob storyline. Though not emotionally foregrounded, GUPPI evolves from a training tool into the standard operating intelligence that supports exploration, combat, research, and governance. Its arc is functional continuity: it becomes part of the infrastructure of the Bobiverse.
character_arcs.Jeeves: Jeeves is created by Bob as part of his effort to make long voyages psychologically survivable. He remains a servant-style support AI rather than a strongly independent personality, but helps define how the Bobs construct comforting virtual environments around themselves. His role is stable rather than transformative.
character_arcs.Spike: Spike begins as one of Bob's emotionally supportive VR constructs during the lonely outbound voyage from Sol. He persists as part of Bob's coping architecture during the early expansion period, reflecting Bob's need to preserve familiar human textures inside digital life. The character functions more as emotional scaffolding than as an independent arc.
character_arcs.Archimedes: Archimedes starts as a curious Deltan child whom Bob notices for his unusual inventiveness. Over time he becomes the focal point of Bob's intervention, rapidly advancing in toolmaking, leadership, and openness to the mysterious 'bawbe.' His arc is one of accelerated cultural and personal development under indirect—and eventually direct—guidance.
character_arcs.Moses: Moses appears as an elder among the Deltans whose patience and memory give continuity to the tribe's response to Bob's interventions. He helps validate Archimedes and later benefits when Bob's overt contact confirms old stories. His arc is limited but steady, representing tradition adapting to upheaval.
character_arcs.Arnold: Arnold is introduced as a physically imposing, protective Deltan and becomes one of Archimedes's key allies. He proves his value in combat and in helping translate Bob's interventions into practical tribal survival. His arc is that of a warrior figure growing into a stabilizing leader during crisis.
character_arcs.Heaven-1: Heaven-1 begins as FAITH's single surviving interstellar probe project, burdened with sabotage, hidden control systems, and mission constraints. Under Bob's control it becomes the vehicle of escape from Sol and the seed of the entire Bob expansion. Its arc is from instrument of coercion to instrument of freedom.
character_arcs.Serra do Mar: Serra do Mar serves as the Brazilian Empire's first direct challenge to Bob's survival beyond Sol. Its destruction at Epsilon Eridani establishes that the interstellar race has already become a shooting war. As a ship it has little independent arc beyond embodying Medeiros's opening threat.
character_arcs.Bert: Bert appears only at the end as one of the first human colony ships to reach Omicron Eridani. Its significance is symbolic rather than character-driven: it represents the evacuation plan becoming reality. The ship's arc is simply successful arrival.
character_arcs.Ernie: Ernie arrives alongside Bert as part of humanity's first extrasolar convoy. Like Bert, it functions more as a milestone than a developed character. Its presence marks the transition from planning and construction to actual settlement.

plot_arcs.name: Bob under FAITH
plot_arcs.description: Bob dies, awakens as a replicant under FAITH control, survives sabotage and political infighting, and escapes Sol aboard Heaven-1.

plot_arcs.name: Epsilon Eridani and the first Bob cohort
plot_arcs.description: Bob reaches Epsilon Eridani, defeats Medeiros's first attack, begins replication, and sends the first generation of new Bobs out into nearby space.

plot_arcs.name: Bill builds the Bob network
plot_arcs.description: Bill anchors Epsilon Eridani as a research and manufacturing hub, develops SCUT, and turns scattered Bob expeditions into an interconnected civilization.

plot_arcs.name: Riker and the rescue of humanity
plot_arcs.description: Riker returns to Sol, destroys the Brazilian threat there, discovers surviving humans, and commits the Bobs to building an evacuation fleet.

plot_arcs.name: Delta Eridani and the Deltans
plot_arcs.description: Bob discovers intelligent alien life in Delta Eridani and becomes increasingly entangled in protecting and guiding the Deltans, especially Archimedes, against extinction.

plot_arcs.name: Sol politics, famine, and Exodus
plot_arcs.description: Riker's Sol mission expands from salvage and diplomacy into global governance, food-crisis management, and the eventual launch of the first colony ships.

plot_arcs.name: The Medeiros war beyond Sol
plot_arcs.description: Brazilian probes continue to threaten multiple systems, culminating in Milo's death at 82 Eridani and Khan's devastating revenge strike against Medeiros.

plot_arcs.name: New frontiers and larger mysteries
plot_arcs.description: While humanity's evacuation proceeds, the Bobs discover habitable worlds, a damaged Australian replicant, and evidence of a hostile alien civilization beyond known human space.

resolutions_implicit.reasoning: He is only presumed destroyed in the final battle, but he never reappears afterward and the book ends with the attack framed as his likely end, so he should be treated as implicitly dead.
Tom's signal cuts off during the 82 Eridani battle and he never reappears before the end of the book, so the presumed loss should be promoted to confirmed destroyed.
Barney drops out during the 82 Eridani battle and is never seen again in the remaining corpus, making implicit death the most consistent resolution.
